name: NC Math 2026
source: North Carolina Standard Course of Study
description: North Carolina's K-12 mathematics standards adopted by the State Board of Education in October 2026, taught from 2028-29: kindergarten to grade 8, NC Mathematics 1 and 2, and three state electives. One topic per standard, with its objectives.

topics.name: Count objects to 20
topics.description: Connect counting with how many objects there are, up to 20. Covers the counting sequence, one-to-one matching, cardinality, writing and showing numerals 0-20, one more, and seeing groups of up to 5 at a glance.
topics.statement: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities when counting objects within 20.

objectives.statement: Count a collection of objects using the correct number sequence within 20.
Demonstrate one-to-one correspondence by matching each object to one spoken number word while keeping track of objects without skipping or double-counting.
Recognize that the last number said when counting is the total number of objects in the set (cardinality).
Represent a counted set of objects with a written numeral 0-20, with 0 representing a count of no objects.
Produce a set of objects that represents the quantity when given a number 0-20.
Identify the next successive number when an object is added, recognizing the quantity is one more/greater.
Write numbers 0-20.
State the number of objects in a group within 5, without counting the objects (perceptual subitizing).

topics.name: Count to 100
topics.description: Use the pattern of the number system to count up to 100. Covers counting by ones and by tens to 100, counting on from any number, and counting back within 10.
topics.statement: Make use of structure in the number system to count within 100.

objectives.statement: Count to 100 by ones.
Count forward by ones from any given number within 100.
Count backward by ones from any given number within 10.
Count to 100 by tens.

topics.name: Compare numbers to 20
topics.description: Describe how two quantities up to 20 relate. Covers comparing sets and numerals as more, fewer or equal, and making sets that are more, fewer or the same.
topics.statement: Reason abstractly and quantitatively to describe relationships between two quantities within 20.

objectives.statement: Compare two sets of objects to determine which has more, fewer, or the same (equal) number of objects within 20.
Produce a set of objects that has more, fewer, or the same (equal) number of objects as a given set within 20.
Compare two numerals to determine which is greater than, less than, or has the same value (equal) within 20.
Produce a set of objects that has more, fewer, or the same (equal) number of objects as a given numeral within 20.

topics.name: Add and subtract within 10
topics.description: Understand addition and subtraction within 10 with objects and drawings. Covers joining and separating, counting on and back, simple word problems, writing + and - expressions, part-part-whole and making 10.
topics.statement: Make sense of addition and subtraction within 10 using objects and drawings.

objectives.statement: Recognize the combination of small groups with totals within 10 without counting (conceptual subitizing).
Demonstrate addition and subtraction situations within 10 using objects by: Joining/adding to quantities; Separating/taking from quantities.
Apply appropriate strategies to add and subtract within 10 using objects or drawings, including: Counting all; Counting on; Counting back; One more, one less; Combinations of 10.

Represent addition and subtraction word problems within 10, using objects or drawings, including the following problem types: Add To/Take From (Result Unknown); Put Together/Take Apart (Total Unknown and Two Addends Unknown).

Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 10, using drawings, numbers, and/or words, including the following problem types: Add To/Take From (Result Unknown); Put Together/Take Apart (Total Unknown and Two Addends Unknown).
Connect composition and decomposition to addition and subtraction by recording written expressions with (+) as a symbol for addition and (-) as a symbol for subtraction.
Apply part-part-whole relationships to compose and decompose numbers within 10 in more than one way using objects or drawings.
Find the number that makes 10 when added to a given number using objects or drawings.

topics.name: Addition and subtraction within 5
topics.description: Build fluency with early addition and subtraction facts. Covers adding and subtracting 0 or 1 within 10 and fluent facts within 5.
topics.statement: Use repeated reasoning to develop fluency with addition and subtraction.

objectives.statement: Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction of 0 or 1 within 10.
Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction within 5.

topics.name: Teen numbers
topics.description: Understand the numbers 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more. Covers composing and decomposing teen numbers with objects, drawings, numbers and expressions.
topics.statement: Make sense of the structure of teen numbers (11-19).

objectives.statement: Compose numbers as a group of ten ones and additional ones using objects and/or drawings.
Decompose numbers as a group of ten ones and additional ones using objects and/or drawings.
Represent the composition and decomposition of teen numbers as a group of ten ones and additional ones with numbers or expressions.

topics.name: Repeating patterns
topics.description: Recognise and build patterns that repeat with colours, shapes, sounds or objects. Covers finding the core unit, extending and creating AB, AAB, ABB and ABC patterns.
topics.statement: Use repeated reasoning to make sense of repeating patterns with colors, shapes, sounds, movements, pictures, or objects.

objectives.statement: Identify the core unit in a repeating pattern (AB, AAB, ABB, ABC).
Extend a repeating pattern (AB, AAB, ABB, ABC) by repeating the core unit two additional times.
Create a repeating pattern (AB, AAB, ABB, ABC).

topics.name: Name and describe shapes
topics.description: Describe flat and solid shapes by their attributes. Covers naming common 2D and 3D shapes in any orientation or size, sorting 2D from 3D, and comparing 2D shapes.
topics.statement: Describe shapes and their attributes.

objectives.statement: Name two-dimensional and three-dimensional shapes, regardless of their orientations or overall size, including triangles, squares, rectangles, hexagons, circles, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres.
Classify shapes as two-dimensional or three-dimensional.
Compare two-dimensional shapes in different sizes and orientations based on their attributes.

topics.name: Draw and build shapes
topics.description: Make two-dimensional shapes. Covers drawing and building triangles, rectangles, squares and circles, and combining shapes into larger figures.
topics.statement: Create two-dimensional shapes.

objectives.statement: Draw triangles, rectangles, squares, and circles.
Build triangles, rectangles, squares, and circles.
Compose two-dimensional figures by combining triangles, rectangles, and/or squares.

topics.name: Compare length, height and weight
topics.description: Compare two objects by an attribute that can be measured. Covers describing length, height and weight and comparing them with words such as longer or heavier.
topics.statement: Compare the measurable attributes of two objects.

objectives.statement: Describe measurable attributes of objects, including length, height, and weight.
Compare two objects using the same measurable attribute, including length, height, and weight, using comparative language.

topics.name: Sort by one attribute
topics.description: Sort and classify objects by a shared attribute. Covers sorting up to 20 objects by one attribute and describing the attribute used.
topics.statement: Use repeated reasoning to sort and classify based on attributes.

objectives.statement: Sort up to 20 pictures and/or objects based on one attribute.
Describe the attribute used to sort a set of objects.

topics.name: Object and picture graphs
topics.description: Use the data cycle with simple object and picture graphs. Covers deciding what data a question needs, collecting it, graphing it, counting and comparing categories, and sharing conclusions.
topics.statement: Apply the data cycle with a focus on simple object graphs and picture graphs.

objectives.statement: Determine the data needed to answer a question posed by the teacher with up to 20 data points within three categories.
Collect categorical data based on a question posed by the teacher.
Represent a data set (vertically or horizontally) by organizing and structuring collected data on an object graph and/or a picture graph.
Count to determine how many are in each category and the total number of data points.
Compare the counts in each category using comparison language, such as more than, less than, and the same (equal) amount.
Communicate observations, conclusions, and/or decisions based on the question posed and data collected.

topics.name: Count to 120
topics.description: Use the structure of the number system to count within 120. Covers counting forward and back by ones and tens, counting by fives, and describing skip-counting patterns.
topics.statement: Make use of structure in the number system to count within 120.

objectives.statement: Count forward from any given number by ones within 120 and by tens within 100.
Count backward from any given number by ones within 120 and by tens within 100.
Count forward by 5s from any multiple of 5 within 100.
Analyze numerical patterns of skip counting sequences by 5s and 10s within 100 to describe how the numbers increase by a constant amount.

topics.name: Count collections to 120
topics.description: Count larger collections of objects by grouping them. Covers grouping strategies to find a total and writing the numeral for a set.
topics.statement: Make use of structure to count objects within 120.

objectives.statement: Count a collection of objects using grouping strategies to determine the total.
Represent a set of objects with a written numeral.

topics.name: Tens and ones
topics.description: Understand two-digit numbers as tens and ones. Covers making a ten from ten ones, composing and decomposing two-digit numbers, and standard and expanded form.
topics.statement: Make use of structure to develop place value understanding for two-digit numbers.

objectives.statement: Unitize a collection of ten ones into a group of ten.
Represent the composition and decomposition of two-digit numbers as groups of tens and additional ones.
Apply place value understanding to read and write numbers in standard and expanded form.

topics.name: Compare numbers to 100
topics.description: Use place value to reason about the size of numbers to 100. Covers numbers on a number line, comparing with >, < and =, and estimating positions from benchmarks.
topics.statement: Make use of place value structure to reason about the magnitude of whole numbers within 100.

objectives.statement: Represent whole numbers as distances from 0 on a pre-marked number line within 20.
Compare numbers within 100 by reasoning about the values of tens and ones digits, the location of the numbers on a number line, and using symbols (>, <, =).
Estimate the location of numbers within 100 on a number line by reasoning about their relationship to benchmark numbers.

topics.name: Add and subtract within 20
topics.description: Understand addition and subtraction within 20. Covers strategies such as counting on, doubles and making ten, word problems with an unknown, and adding three numbers using properties.
topics.statement: Make sense of addition and subtraction within 20.

objectives.statement: Apply appropriate strategies to add and subtract within 20, including: Counting on/back; Using doubles/near doubles; Making ten/decomposing a number leading to a ten; Using the relationship between addition and subtraction; Creating equivalent sums or differences; Using the commutative property.

Represent addition and subtraction word problems within 20, using equations with a symbol for the unknown number, including the following problem types: Add To/Take From (Change Unknown); Put Together/Take Apart (Addend Unknown); Compare (Difference Unknown).

Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 20, using representations, including the following problem types: Add To/Take From (Change Unknown); Put Together/Take Apart (Addend Unknown); Compare (Difference Unknown).
Apply the commutative and associative properties to solve addition problems within 20 involving three addends with and without context.

topics.name: Addition facts within 10
topics.description: Build fluency with the foundational addition and subtraction facts. Covers fluent facts within 10, ten-plus facts and doubles within 20.
topics.statement: Use repeated reasoning to develop fluency with addition and subtraction foundational facts.

objectives.statement: Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction within 10.
Demonstrate fluency with 10 plus (10 + __) facts and doubles within 20.

topics.name: The equal sign
topics.description: Use the equal sign to describe how quantities within 20 relate. Covers the meaning of =, deciding whether two expressions are equal, and finding an unknown in any position.
topics.statement: Apply understanding of the equal sign to explain the relationship between quantities within 20 by reasoning abstractly and quantitatively.

objectives.statement: Describe the equal sign (=) as showing the quantities on both sides have the same value.
Justify whether two addition and/or subtraction expressions within 20 are equal or not equal using representations.
Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation with the unknown in all positions.

topics.name: Add and subtract within 100
topics.description: Use place value to add and subtract within 100. Covers adding and subtracting one-digit numbers and multiples of 10, explaining strategies, and finding 10 more or 10 less mentally.
topics.statement: Make use of place value structure to add and subtract within 100 with and without context.

objectives.statement: Apply place value strategies and/or properties of operations using representations to add and subtract a two-digit number and a one-digit number.
Apply place value strategies and/or properties of operations using representations to add and subtract a two-digit number and a multiple of 10.
Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work based on place value and/or number relationships within 100.
Apply place value understanding to mentally determine 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number, without having to count.

topics.name: Attributes of shapes
topics.description: Describe and create shapes from their defining attributes. Covers defining versus non-defining attributes, sides and vertices, drawing 2D shapes, and naming, building and comparing 3D shapes.
topics.statement: Make use of structure to describe and create shapes based on their defining attributes.

objectives.statement: Distinguish between defining and non-defining attributes of triangles, rectangles, squares, hexagons, and circles.
Describe triangles, rectangles, squares, hexagons, and circles based on their defining attributes, including the number of sides, vertices, and angles.
Draw triangles, rectangles, squares, hexagons, and circles.

Name three-dimensional shapes, including cubes, rectangular prisms, spheres, cones, and cylinders, using the shapes of their faces and whether their surfaces are flat or curved as defining attributes.
Build three-dimensional shapes, including cubes, rectangular prisms, spheres, cones, and cylinders.
Compare cubes, rectangular prisms, spheres, cones, and cylinders by describing the shapes of their faces and whether their surfaces are flat or curved.

topics.name: Halves and fourths
topics.description: Understand equal shares of a whole as halves and fourths. Covers partitioning circles and rectangles, naming the shares, and why fourths are smaller than halves.
topics.statement: Make sense of the relationship between a whole and its equal shares (halves and fourths) in real-world situations.

objectives.statement: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares.
Describe equal shares of circles and rectangles as halves and fourths, using the language “half of” and “fourth of.”
Describe a whole as two halves or four fourths.
Explain why partitioning the same whole into four equal parts creates smaller pieces than partitioning it into two equal parts.

topics.name: Compare and order lengths
topics.description: Reason about length without standard units. Covers ordering three objects by length and comparing two lengths using a third object.
topics.statement: Reason about length using non-standard units.

objectives.statement: Order three objects by length.
Compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

topics.name: Measure with non-standard units
topics.description: Measure lengths by repeating a smaller unit. Covers expressing length as a whole number of units laid end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
topics.statement: Measure lengths using non-standard units.

objectives.statement: Express the length of an object as a whole number of non-standard length units.
Measure by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end (iterating) with no gaps or overlaps.

topics.name: Time to the half hour
topics.description: Tell time to the nearest hour and half hour. Covers hours and minutes on a clock and reading analog and digital clocks.
topics.statement: Tell time to the nearest hour and half-hour.

objectives.statement: Describe units of time represented on a clock as minutes and hours.
Determine time to the nearest hour and half-hour using analog and digital clocks.

topics.name: Value of coins
topics.description: Understand what coins are worth. Covers identifying quarters, dimes, nickels and pennies, their values, and counting collections of like coins to 100 cents.
topics.statement: Develop an understanding of the value of coins.

objectives.statement: Identify quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies.
Determine the value of quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies.
Count by 1s, 5s, or 10s to determine the value of a collection of like coins (pennies, nickels, or dimes) up to 100 cents.

topics.name: Sort by one or two attributes
topics.description: Sort and classify objects by how they are alike and different. Covers sorting up to 20 objects by one or two attributes and describing the attributes used.
topics.statement: Use repeated reasoning to sort and classify objects based on similarities and differences.

objectives.statement: Sort up to 20 pictures and/or objects based on one or two attributes.
Describe the attribute(s) used to sort a set of objects.

topics.name: Data with picture graphs
topics.description: Use the data cycle with object and picture graphs. Covers asking questions that need categorical data, collecting up to 20 data points, graphing them, and drawing and sharing conclusions.
topics.statement: Apply the data cycle with a focus on object graphs and picture graphs.

objectives.statement: Generate questions, within a given context, that require the collection of categorical data.
Determine the data needed to answer a posed question with up to 20 data points within four categories.
Collect categorical data using various methods to answer a question.
Represent a data set (vertically or horizontally) by organizing and structuring collected data on an object graph and/or picture graph.
Analyze categorical data to describe, compare, and draw conclusions.
Communicate observations, conclusions, and/or decisions based on the question posed and data collected.

topics.name: Skip counting, odd and even
topics.description: Use patterns in numbers to reason about quantities. Covers counting by 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s and 100s within 1,000, odd and even numbers, and totals of small arrays.
topics.statement: Apply patterns and structure in numbers to reason about quantities.

objectives.statement: Solve problems, with and without context, by counting forward and backward by 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s, and 100s from any given number within 1,000.

Determine whether a group within 20 has an odd or even number of objects using strategies such as pairing objects and counting by 2s, forming two equal groups, and/or expressing an even number as a sum of two equal addends in an equation.
Determine the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns using skip-counting and/or repeated addition.

topics.name: Hundreds, tens and ones
topics.description: Understand three-digit numbers through place value. Covers making a hundred from ten tens, the value of each digit, equivalent forms, and standard, expanded and word form.
topics.statement: Make use of structure to develop place value understanding for three-digit numbers.

objectives.statement: Unitize a collection of ten tens into a group of a hundred.
Represent the composition and decomposition of three-digit numbers as groups of hundreds, groups of tens, and additional ones.
Apply place value understanding to determine the value of each digit in a three-digit number.
Apply place value reasoning to compose and decompose numbers within 200 to show equivalent forms using representations.
Apply place value understanding to read and write numbers within 1,000 in standard, expanded, and word form.

topics.name: Compare numbers to 1,000
topics.description: Use place value to reason about the size of numbers within 1,000. Covers comparing and ordering with digits, number lines and symbols, and estimating positions on a number line.
topics.statement: Make use of place value structure to reason about magnitude of whole numbers within 1,000.

objectives.statement: Apply place value understanding to compare and order numbers within 1,000, by: Reasoning about the values of hundreds, tens, and ones digits; Reasoning about the location of the numbers on a number line; Representing comparisons using symbols (>, <, =).
Estimate the location of numbers within 1,000 on a number line by reasoning about their relationship to benchmark numbers.

topics.name: Mental addition and subtraction
topics.description: Build fluency with mental addition and subtraction. Covers fluent facts within 20 and adding or subtracting 10 or 100 within 1,000.
topics.statement: Use repeated reasoning to develop fluency with addition and subtraction using mental strategies.

objectives.statement: Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction within 20.
Apply place value understanding within 1,000, to add 10 or 100 and subtract 10 or 100.

topics.name: Add and subtract within 100
topics.description: Add and subtract fluently within 100 using place value and properties. Covers strategies, one- and two-step word problems with an unknown, and choosing efficient strategies.
topics.statement: Make use of place value structure and properties of operations to fluently add and subtract within 100.

objectives.statement: Apply appropriate strategies to fluently add and subtract within 100, including: Composing and decomposing numbers based on place value; Commutative and associative properties; Relationship between addition and subtraction; Creating equivalent sums or differences.

Represent one-step addition and subtraction word problems within 100, using equations with a symbol for the unknown number, including the following problem types: Add To/Take From (Start Unknown); Compare (Bigger Unknown); Compare (Smaller Unknown).

Represent two-step addition and subtraction word problems within 100, using equations with a symbol for the unknown number, including the following problem types: Add To/Take From (Change Unknown); Add To/Take From (Result Unknown).

Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction word problems within 100, using place value understanding, commutative and associative properties of addition, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
Analyze number relationships to justify efficient strategy selection for addition and subtraction.

topics.name: Equal and not equal within 100
topics.description: Use the equal sign to compare quantities and expressions within 100. Covers justifying whether two expressions are equal and finding an unknown in any position.
topics.statement: Apply understanding of the equal sign to explain the relationship between quantities and expressions as equal or not equal within 100.

objectives.statement: Justify whether two addition and/or subtraction expressions within 100 are equal or not equal using representations.
Determine the unknown whole number in addition or subtraction equations within 100 with the unknown in all positions.

topics.name: Add and subtract within 1,000
topics.description: Use place value and properties to add and subtract within 1,000. Covers adding three two-digit numbers, adding and subtracting three-digit numbers, and explaining why strategies work.
topics.statement: Make use of place value structure and properties of operations to add and subtract within 1,000 with and without context.

objectives.statement: Apply place value strategies and/or properties of operations using representations to add three two-digit numbers by: Composing and decomposing numbers; Using the commutative and associative properties of addition; Creating equivalent sums.

Apply place value strategies and/or properties of operations using representations to add and subtract within 1,000 by: Composing and decomposing numbers; Using the commutative and associative properties of addition; Using the relationship between addition and subtraction; Creating equivalent sums and differences.
Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work based on place value and/or number relationships within 1,000.

topics.name: Two-dimensional shapes
topics.description: Reason about flat shapes and their attributes. Covers comparing polygons and circles by sides, vertices and angles, composing and decomposing shapes, and lines of symmetry.
topics.statement: Reason with two-dimensional shapes and their attributes.

objectives.statement: Compare triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, octagons, and circles based on the number of sides, vertices, and angles.
Describe the attributes of the new shape when composing three or more two-dimensional shapes.
Identify the individual shapes created when decomposing a two-dimensional figure.
Justify whether a shape or composite figure has a line of symmetry.

topics.name: Halves, thirds and fourths
topics.description: Understand equal shares of a whole as halves, thirds and fourths. Covers partitioning circles and rectangles, naming shares, equal shares that look different, and more shares meaning smaller shares.
topics.statement: Make sense of the relationship between a whole and its equal shares (halves, thirds, fourths) in real-world situations.

objectives.statement: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, and four equal shares.
Describe equal shares of circles and rectangles as halves, thirds, and fourths, using the language “half of,” “third of,” “fourth of,” and “quarter of."
Describe a whole as two halves, three thirds, or four fourths.
Explain why equal shares of the same whole may look different but represent equal amounts.
Explain why partitioning the same whole into more equal shares results in smaller shares.

topics.name: Measure length in units
topics.description: Measure and estimate length in customary and metric units. Covers measuring with rulers and tapes, comparing measurements in two units, choosing a unit, estimating and comparing lengths.
topics.statement: Apply understanding of customary and metric units to reason about length.

objectives.statement: Measure object length to the nearest customary unit (inch, foot, yard) and metric unit (centimeter, meter) using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.
Measure the same object with two different units within the same system (customary or metric) to explain how the size of the unit chosen relates to the length measurement of the object.
Choose an appropriate customary unit (inch, foot, yard) or metric unit (centimeter, meter) to measure the length of an object.
Estimate length with customary units (inches, feet, yards) or metric units (centimeters, meters) using measurement benchmarks.
Measure to compare the lengths of two objects.

topics.name: Time to the minute
topics.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute. Covers reading and writing times to 5 minutes and 1 minute on analog and digital clocks with a.m. and p.m.
topics.statement: Develop an understanding of time to the nearest minute.

objectives.statement: Tell time to the nearest 5 minutes and 1 minute on analog and digital clocks, using a.m. and p.m. appropriately.
Write times shown on analog and digital clocks to the nearest 5 minutes and 1 minute, using a.m. and p.m. appropriately.

topics.name: Count money to $1
topics.description: Work with the value of coins up to one dollar. Covers making a given amount with coins and finding the value of a set of mixed coins.
topics.statement: Apply understanding of the value of money using coins.

objectives.statement: Compose a set of coins to match a given amount within 100 cents ($1.00).
Determine the value of a given combination of quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies within 100 cents ($1.00).

topics.name: Sort up to 30 objects
topics.description: Sort and classify objects by one or two attributes. Covers sorting up to 30 objects and describing the attributes used.
topics.statement: Use repeated reasoning to sort and classify objects based on one or two attributes.

objectives.statement: Sort up to 30 pictures and/or objects based on one or two attributes.
Describe the attribute(s) used to sort a set of objects.

topics.name: Picture and bar graphs
topics.description: Use the data cycle with single-scale picture and bar graphs. Covers posing questions, collecting up to 30 data points, graphing them, and analysing and sharing conclusions.
topics.statement: Apply the data cycle with a focus on single-scaled picture and bar graphs.

objectives.statement: Generate questions, within a given context, that require the collection of categorical data.
Determine the data needed to answer a posed question with up to 30 data points within four categories.
Collect categorical data using various methods to answer a question.
Represent a data set (vertically or horizontally) by organizing and structuring collected data on a picture graph and/or bar graph.
Analyze categorical data to describe, compare, and draw conclusions.
Communicate observations, conclusions, and/or decisions based on the question posed and data collected.

topics.name: Place value to 10,000
topics.description: Extend place value to numbers within 10,000. Covers the value of each digit, standard, expanded and word forms, equivalent forms, mentally adding multiples of 10, 100 or 1,000, and comparing and ordering.
topics.statement: Make use of structure to extend and apply place value.

objectives.statement: Apply place value understanding to read, write, and determine the place and value of each digit in a whole number within 10,000.
Make connections between different forms, including standard, expanded, and word forms of whole numbers within 10,000.
Apply place value reasoning to compose and decompose numbers within 1,000 to show equivalent forms using representations.
Apply place value reasoning to fluently add or subtract multiples of 10, 100, or 1,000 to a given number within 10,000 using mental strategies.
Apply place value understanding to compare and order whole numbers within 10,000 with representations using symbols (>, <, =, ≠) and/or words to record the results of comparisons.

topics.name: Add and subtract within 1,000
topics.description: Understand whole-number addition and subtraction within 1,000. Covers one-step problems in context, strategies based on expanded form and properties, and building procedural fluency.
topics.statement: Make sense of whole number addition and subtraction within 1,000.

objectives.statement: Apply addition and subtraction strategies to represent and solve one-step problems in context with whole numbers within 1,000.
Apply reasoning strategies to add and subtract within 1,000, including expanded form, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.
Analyze addition and subtraction strategies to develop procedural fluency.

topics.name: Meaning of multiplication
topics.description: Understand multiplication of whole numbers. Covers factors as equal groups, strategies such as skip-counting and decomposing, word problems with equal groups and arrays, patterns, and multiplying by multiples of 10.
topics.statement: Make sense of multiplication with whole numbers.

objectives.statement: Interpret factors as representing the number of equal groups and the number of objects in each group for products of whole numbers with two factors within 10.
Represent strategies, including repeated addition, skip-counting, decomposing a factor, and the commutative property, for products of whole numbers with two factors within 10.
Apply multiplication strategies using representations to solve one-step multiplication word problems with factors within 10, including the following problem types: Equal Groups; Arrays & Area.
Connect multiplication problems in context with equations using a symbol for the unknown number.
Describe patterns of multiplication using visual tools such as hundred boards, multiplication tables, two-column tables, and number lines.
Find the product of a one-digit whole number by a multiple of 10 in the range 10–90 by using representations, based on place value and the properties of operations.

topics.name: Meaning of division
topics.description: Understand division of whole numbers. Covers divisor and quotient as groups and group size, division strategies, word problems with equal groups and arrays, and equations with an unknown.
topics.statement: Make sense of division with whole numbers.

objectives.statement: Interpret the divisor and quotient within 10 in a division equation as representing the number of equal groups and the number of objects in each group.
Represent strategies, including repeated addition or subtraction, skip-counting, and decomposing a factor, for division with a divisor and quotient within 10.

Apply division strategies using representations to solve one-step division word problems involving a divisor and quotient within 10, including the following problem types: Equal Groups; Arrays & Area.
Connect division problems in context with equations using a symbol for the unknown number.

topics.name: Multiplication and division facts
topics.description: Connect multiplication and division. Covers explaining the operations in context, inverse relationships, equal expressions, fluency with facts to 10 x 10, and instant recall of 0s, 1s, 2s, 5s and 10s.
topics.statement: Reason quantitatively to make connections between multiplication and division with whole numbers.

objectives.statement: Construct an argument to explain the connection of a multiplication or division problem in context to the meaning of the operations.
Apply the inverse relationship between multiplication and division.
Justify whether two multiplication and/or division expressions within 100 are equal or not equal using representations.

Develop fluency with multiplication facts through 10 × 10 and the corresponding division facts by applying reasoning strategies (e.g., doubling, add-a-group, subtract-a-group, near squares, and inverse relationships).
Recall foundational multiplication facts (0s, 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s) with automaticity.

topics.name: Two-step word problems
topics.description: Solve problems that use whole-number operations. Covers two-step problems with addition, subtraction and multiplication, and estimating answers.
topics.statement: Make sense and persevere in solving problems involving whole-number operations.

objectives.statement: Apply addition, subtraction, and multiplication strategies to represent and solve two-step problems in context.
Estimate sums, differences, products, and quotients in one- and two-step problems in context.

topics.name: Understand fractions
topics.description: Make sense of fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8. Covers unit fractions, numerators on area models and number lines, equivalent fractions, wholes as fractions, and comparing fractions.
topics.statement: Make sense of fractions.

objectives.statement: Explain that a unit fraction is one part formed when a whole is partitioned into equal parts using denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Identify unit fractions using area and length models with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Explain with an area model that the numerator of a fraction represents the number of equal parts of the unit fraction using fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Explain with a number line that the numerator of a fraction represents the number of lengths of the unit fraction from 0 using fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Determine equivalent fractions by composing and decomposing with area and length models using related fractions: halves, fourths, and eighths; thirds and sixths.
Explain that a fraction with the same numerator and denominator equals one whole using fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Demonstrate equivalency of whole numbers up to 4 using fractions greater than 1 with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole using related fractions: halves, fourths, and eighths; thirds and sixths.

Reason about the size of fractions to compare and order fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator using area and length models, and using symbols (>, <, =) with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.

topics.name: Lines, angles and quadrilaterals
topics.description: Reason about quadrilaterals and their parts. Covers points, lines, segments, parallel and perpendicular lines, types of angles, and identifying kinds of quadrilaterals.
topics.statement: Reason with quadrilaterals and their attributes.

objectives.statement: Construct points, lines, line segments, and perpendicular and parallel lines.
Identify points, lines, line segments, and perpendicular and parallel lines within two-dimensional figures and in context.
Describe angles as geometric shapes that are formed when two rays share a common endpoint.
Identify angles as acute, obtuse, right, or straight based on the relationship to perpendicular or straight lines.
Construct examples and non-examples of quadrilaterals.
Identify types of quadrilaterals, including parallelograms, rhombuses, rectangles, squares, and trapezoids based on their attributes.

topics.name: Time and customary measurement
topics.description: Work with elapsed time and customary units. Covers time intervals within an hour, estimating and measuring length, capacity and weight, and one-step measurement problems.
topics.statement: Make sense of time and customary measurement.

objectives.statement: Solve problems in context involving addition and subtraction of time intervals within the same hour to find an end time, amount of time passed, or a start time.
Estimate customary measurements of length, capacity, and weight using measurement benchmarks.
Measure lengths in customary units to the quarter-inch and half-inch, and feet and yards to the whole unit.
Measure capacity in customary units with cups, pints, quarts, and gallons.
Measure weight in customary units with ounces and pounds.
Solve one-step problems in context involving whole-number measurements of length, weight, and capacity within the same customary units using the four operations.

topics.name: Area and perimeter
topics.description: Understand area and perimeter. Covers area by tiling and multiplying side lengths, splitting rectangles to find area, perimeter of polygons, and finding a missing side from the perimeter.
topics.statement: Make sense of area and perimeter.

objectives.statement: Measure the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling without gaps or overlaps and counting unit squares.
Find the area of rectangles with whole-number side lengths, including problems in context.
Find the area of a rectangle by partitioning it into two smaller rectangles where the area of the large rectangle is the sum of the two smaller rectangles by using tiles and/or arrays.
Find the perimeter of polygons with no more than 8 sides, including problems in context, by measuring the distance around a shape in length units.
Apply understandings of the attributes of quadrilaterals and regular polygons to find the length of an unknown side when given the perimeter.

topics.name: Scaled bar graphs
topics.description: Use the data cycle with frequency tables, scaled bar graphs and picture graphs. Covers posing questions, planning and collecting categorical data, graphing it, and drawing conclusions and predictions.
topics.statement: Apply the data cycle with a focus on frequency tables, scaled bar graphs, and picture graphs.

objectives.statement: Generate questions that require the collection of categorical data.
Determine the data needed to answer a posed question with up to 5 categories.
Design a plan to collect categorical data to answer a question.
Collect categorical data using various methods to answer a question.
Represent a data set (vertically or horizontally) by organizing and structuring collected data on a frequency table, scaled bar graph, and/or picture graph.
Analyze categorical data to describe, compare, draw conclusions, and construct arguments supported by evidence from the data.
Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning to generalize and make predictions based on patterns in the data.

topics.name: Place value to 100,000
topics.description: Extend place value to numbers within 100,000. Covers the value of each digit, equivalent forms, each place being ten times the place to its right, and comparing and ordering.
topics.statement: Make use of structure to extend and apply place value.

objectives.statement: Apply place value understanding to read, write, and determine the place and value of each digit in a whole number within 100,000.
Make connections between equivalent forms of whole numbers, including non-traditional, standard, expanded, and word forms within 100,000.
Apply the patterns of the base-ten system to explain that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right within 100,000.
Apply place value understanding to compare and order whole numbers within 100,000 using symbols (>, <, =, ≠) and/or words to record the results of comparisons.

topics.name: Add and subtract with algorithms
topics.description: Add and subtract whole numbers within 100,000. Covers connecting earlier strategies to the standard algorithm and using it with multi-digit numbers.
topics.statement: Use repeated reasoning to make sense of whole number addition and subtraction within 100,000.

objectives.statement: Connect addition and subtraction strategies within 1,000, including expanded form, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction to the standard algorithm.
Apply place value understanding of the standard algorithm to add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers within 100,000.

topics.name: Multiply and divide whole numbers
topics.description: Understand multiplication and division of whole numbers. Covers factor pairs, primes and composites, multiples, fact fluency to 10 x 10, multiplicative comparison, multi-digit products and quotients, and remainders.
topics.statement: Make sense of multiplication and division with whole numbers.

objectives.statement: Generate factor pairs for a whole number within 50 using representations.
Determine whether a whole number within 50 is prime, composite, or neither.
Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors.
Determine whether a given whole number is a multiple of a given one-digit number.
Demonstrate fluency with multiplication facts through 10 x 10 with reasoning strategies.
Recall multiplication facts through 10 x 10 with automaticity.
Distinguish multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.
Apply multiplication and division strategies using representations to solve one-step multiplication and division word problems with factors within 10, including the following problem types: Compare.

Apply place value strategies and/or the properties of multiplication, to multiply a whole number of up to three digits by a one-digit whole number or up to two two-digit whole numbers using visual and/or symbolic representations, including the area model.

Apply place value strategies, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division to find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to three-digit dividends and one-digit divisors using visual and/or symbolic representations.
Interpret the meaning of the remainder when solving up to three-digit by one-digit division problems in context.

topics.name: Two-step problems, all operations
topics.description: Solve two-step problems with whole numbers. Covers problems with all four operations, equations with a letter for the unknown, and checking answers by estimation.
topics.statement: Make sense and persevere in solving two-step problems involving operations with whole numbers.

objectives.statement: Solve two-step problems in context involving the four operations using a variety of representations, including equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity.
Justify that an answer is reasonable using estimation strategies.

topics.name: Equivalent fractions and decimals
topics.description: Make sense of fractions and decimals. Covers equivalent fractions, comparing and ordering fractions with benchmarks and models, tenths and hundredths as decimals, and comparing decimals.
topics.statement: Make sense of fractions and decimals.

objectives.statement: Explain why a fraction is equivalent to another fraction using area and length models with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100.
Apply reasoning about the size of fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100 to compare and order fractions using area and length models, and using symbols (>, <, =).
Apply reasoning about benchmark fractions 0, ½, and one whole to compare and order fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100 using symbols (>, <, =).

Apply reasoning about equivalent fractions using related fractions: halves, fourths, and eighths; thirds, sixths, and twelfths; fifths, tenths, and hundredths to compare and order fractions using symbols (>, <, =).
Represent decimals less than 2 wholes using tenths and hundredths with visual and/or symbolic representations, making connections between fractions and decimals.
Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole.
Apply place value reasoning to compare and order decimals to the hundredths place using area and length models and symbols (>, <, =).

topics.name: Add fractions, multiply by whole numbers
topics.description: Operate with fractions. Covers adding and subtracting fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, decomposing fractions, multiplying a fraction by a whole number, and fractions of a set.
topics.statement: Make sense of operations with fractions.

objectives.statement: Apply area models, length models, and equations to represent the addition and subtraction of fractions with like denominators as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole using fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100.

Decompose a fraction into a sum of unit fractions and a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way using area models, length models, and equations using fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100.

Apply understanding of properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction to add and subtract fractions, including mixed numbers, with like denominators of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100.
Solve one- and two-step problems in context involving addition and subtraction of fractions, including mixed numbers, with like denominators of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100.
Explain using area and length models that fractions can be represented by multiplying a whole number within 12 by a unit fraction with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, and 12.
Apply understanding of multiplying a whole number within 12 by a unit fraction to multiplying a whole number by any fraction less than one with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, and 12.
Determine a fraction of a set using set models and arrays by multiplying a fraction with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, and 12 by a whole number within 12.
Solve one-step problems in context involving multiplication of fractions and whole numbers, with whole numbers within 12 and denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, and 12.

topics.name: Shape and number patterns
topics.description: Reason about patterns. Covers generating a pattern from a rule, finding the rule of a pattern, and telling growing patterns from repeating ones.
topics.statement: Reason about patterns.

objectives.statement: Generate a shape or number pattern that follows a given rule.
Analyze the relationships in a shape or number pattern to determine the rule.
Analyze a pattern to determine if it is a growing or a repeating pattern to extend the pattern, including problems in context.

topics.name: Measure angles
topics.description: Reason about angles and how they are measured. Covers degrees as parts of a circle, estimating angles, using a protractor, and finding unknown angles by adding and subtracting.
topics.statement: Reason about angles and their measurement.

objectives.statement: Demonstrate an understanding that angles are measured in degrees with reference to the degrees of a circle.
Estimate angle measurements using types of angles (acute, obtuse, right, or straight) and angle benchmarks.
Use a protractor to measure angles in whole-number degrees.
Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram or in one- or two-step problems in context.

topics.name: Classify triangles and quadrilaterals
topics.description: Reason about triangles and quadrilaterals by their attributes. Covers notation for points, lines and rays, classifying triangles by angles and sides, and classifying quadrilaterals.
topics.statement: Reason with triangles and quadrilaterals and their attributes.

objectives.statement: Construct points, lines, rays, angles, and parallel and perpendicular lines using symbolic notation within two-dimensional figures and in context.
Construct examples of triangles based on angle types (obtuse, right, acute) and side lengths (equilateral, isosceles, scalene), including cross-classifying.
Name triangles based on angle types (obtuse, right, acute) and side lengths (equilateral, isosceles, scalene), including cross-classifying.
Classify quadrilaterals and triangles based on angle measure, side lengths, and the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines.

topics.name: Time and metric measurement
topics.description: Work with elapsed time and metric units. Covers time intervals across the hour, estimating and measuring length, capacity and mass, one-step problems, and converting larger units to smaller.
topics.statement: Make sense of time and metric measurement.

objectives.statement: Solve problems in context involving addition and subtraction of time intervals that cross over the hour to find an end time, amount of time passed, or a start time.
Estimate metric measurements of length, capacity, and weight using measurement benchmarks.
Measure lengths in metric units with centimeters and meters.
Measure capacity in metric units with liters and milliliters.
Measure weight in metric units with grams and kilograms.
Solve one-step problems in context involving whole-number measurements of length, weight, and capacity that are given within the same metric unit using the four operations.

Use place value understanding and representations, including tables, to apply multiplicative reasoning to convert metric measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit with a given conversion chart.

topics.name: Area and perimeter formulas
topics.description: Apply area and perimeter in problems. Covers the rectangle formulas in context, area of rectilinear figures, and fixed area with changing perimeter and the reverse.
topics.statement: Reason abstractly and quantitatively to apply understandings of area and perimeter.

objectives.statement: Apply the area and perimeter formulas of rectangles to solve problems in context.
Find the area of rectilinear figures with known side lengths composed of two or three non-overlapping rectangles.
Solve problems in context involving a fixed area and varying perimeters or a fixed perimeter and varying areas of rectangles.

topics.name: Line plots and double bar graphs
topics.description: Use the data cycle with frequency tables, line plots and bar graphs. Covers categorical and numerical questions, collecting and graphing data, range, mode and median, and drawing conclusions.
topics.statement: Apply the data cycle with a focus on frequency tables, line plots, and single and double bar graphs.

objectives.statement: Generate questions that require the collection of categorical or numerical data.
Determine whether a question will yield categorical or numerical data.
Design a plan to collect categorical or numerical data to answer a question.
Collect categorical or numerical data using various methods to answer a question.
Represent a data set by organizing and structuring collected data on a frequency table, line plot, or single and double bar graph.
Make sense of the range as a measure of spread and the mode as the most common value in a data set.
Make sense of the median as the middle value of the data set.
Analyze categorical or numerical data to describe, compare, draw conclusions, and construct arguments supported by evidence from the data.
Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning to generalize and make predictions based on patterns in the data.

topics.name: Numerical expressions
topics.description: Make sense of numerical expressions. Covers order of operations in two-step expressions, relating expressions to properties, and connecting them to representations.
topics.statement: Make sense of numerical expressions.

objectives.statement: Evaluate two-step numerical expressions by applying the order of operations.
Explain numerical expressions by relating them to the commutative, associative, and distributive properties.
Connect numerical expressions to a variety of representations.

topics.name: Place value and decimals
topics.description: Extend place value to millions and thousandths. Covers the value of each digit, forms of decimals, patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of ten, and comparing decimals.
topics.statement: Make use of structure to extend and apply place value.

objectives.statement: Apply place value understanding to read, write, and determine the place and value of each digit in a whole number within one million.
Apply place value understanding to read, write, and determine the place and value of each digit in decimal numbers to the thousandths place.
Make connections between equivalent forms, including standard, expanded, and word forms of decimal numbers to the thousandths place.
Explain patterns in products and quotients when numbers are multiplied by 1,000, 100, 10, 0.1, and 0.01 and/or divided by 10 and 100.

Apply the patterns within the base-ten system from the thousandth place through one million to explain that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and ⅒ of what it represents in the place to its left.
Apply place value understanding to compare and order decimal numbers to the thousandths, using symbols (>, <, =, ≠) and/or words to record the results of comparisons.

topics.name: Multi-digit multiplication and division
topics.description: Operate with multi-digit whole numbers. Covers multiplying three-digit by two-digit numbers, dividing four-digit by one-digit numbers including long division, remainders, multi-step problems and estimation.
topics.statement: Use repeated reasoning to operate with multi-digit numbers.

objectives.statement: Apply place value reasoning and/or the properties of multiplication to multiply up to a three-digit by a two-digit whole number using symbolic and/or visual representations, including the area model and the standard algorithm.

Apply place value strategies, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division to find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors using visual and/or symbolic representations.
Connect previous understandings and strategies to develop the algorithm, including long division, to divide whole numbers up to a four-digit dividend with a one-digit divisor.
Interpret the meaning of the remainder when solving up to four-digit by one-digit division problems in context.
Solve multi-step problems in context involving the four operations using whole numbers.
Justify that an answer is reasonable using estimation strategies.

topics.name: Operations with decimals
topics.description: Make sense of operations with decimals. Covers adding and subtracting to thousandths, multiplying and dividing by a whole number within 4, two-step problems, and estimation.
topics.statement: Make sense of operations with decimal numbers.

objectives.statement: Solve addition and subtraction problems up to six total digits and numbers to the thousandths place using visual and symbolic representations.
Multiply a whole number within 4 and a decimal to the hundredths place using visual and symbolic representations.
Divide a whole number within 4 and a decimal to the hundredths place using visual and symbolic representations.
Solve two-step problems in context involving two operations with decimal numbers.
Justify an answer is reasonable using estimation strategies.

topics.name: Operations with fractions
topics.description: Make sense of operations with fractions. Covers adding and subtracting with unlike denominators, fractions as division, multiplying fractions, scaling, and dividing with unit fractions.
topics.statement: Make sense of operations with fractions.

objectives.statement: Apply understanding of equivalent fractions, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction to add and subtract fractions using representations, including mixed numbers, with unlike denominators using related fractions: halves, fourths, and eighths; thirds, sixths, and twelfths; fifths, tenths, and hundredths.

Solve one- and two-step problems in context involving addition and subtraction of fractions, including mixed numbers, with unlike denominators using related fractions: halves, fourths, and eighths; thirds, sixths, and twelfths; fifths, tenths, and hundredths.
Interpret a fraction as the division of the numerator by the denominator with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, and 12, using area, length, and set models, equal sharing contexts, and equations.
Multiply a whole number within 12 by a fraction or a mixed number with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, and 12 using representations.
Multiply two fractions or mixed numbers within 12 with denominators 2, 3, and 4 using representations.

Explain why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number and when multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number.

Divide unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and divide whole numbers within 10 by unit fractions that include denominators of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, and 12, using area and/or length models and equations.

topics.name: Patterns and relationships
topics.description: Reason about patterns and how they relate. Covers generating two patterns from rules and analysing the relationship between corresponding terms.
topics.statement: Reason with patterns and relationships.

objectives.statement: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules.
Analyze the relationships between corresponding terms in two patterns using words and numerical expressions.
Analyze the relationships between terms and patterns in problems in context.

topics.name: Hierarchy of quadrilaterals
topics.description: Reason about shapes through their properties. Covers classifying quadrilaterals in a hierarchy and how attributes carry to subcategories.
topics.statement: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

objectives.statement: Classify quadrilaterals in a hierarchy based on properties.
Explain that attributes belonging to a category of quadrilaterals also belong to all subcategories of that category.

topics.name: The coordinate plane
topics.description: Reason about location in the first quadrant. Covers graphing points, solving problems on the plane, and graphing ordered pairs from patterns.
topics.statement: Reason about location and patterns in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.

objectives.statement: Graph points on a coordinate plane.
Solve problems on a coordinate plane, including traveling from one point to another and identifying the coordinates of missing points in geometric figures.
Create ordered pairs using corresponding terms that follow given rules to graph points on a coordinate plane.
Solve problems in context using the patterns graphed on a coordinate plane.

topics.name: Convert measurement units
topics.description: Convert between units within the customary or the metric system. Covers checking that conversions are reasonable and solving one- or two-step conversion problems.
topics.statement: Reason abstractly and quantitatively to apply understandings of customary and metric measurement.

objectives.statement: Justify the reasonableness of metric and customary unit conversions within a given measurement system in context.

Apply multiplicative reasoning to solve one- or two-step problems in context involving conversions between two units within the customary system (inches, feet, yards, ounces, pounds, fluid ounces, cups, pints, quarts, gallons, minutes, hours) with a given conversion and technology.

Apply multiplicative reasoning to solve one- or two-step problems in context involving conversions between two units within the metric system (millimeters, centimeters, meters, kilometers, milligram, gram, kilogram, milliliter, liter) with a given conversion and technology.

topics.name: Volume of rectangular prisms
topics.description: Understand and apply volume of rectangular prisms. Covers volume in cubic units, packing with unit cubes, the volume formula, finding a missing dimension, and composite prisms.
topics.statement: Reason abstractly and quantitatively to apply understandings of volume of rectangular prisms.

objectives.statement: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures by filling rectangular prisms using cubic units, cubic centimeters, cubic inches, and cubic feet.
Find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes.

Connect the operations of multiplication and addition to the volume formula for a rectangular prism, by modeling that volume can be found by multiplying the edge lengths or by multiplying the area of the base by the height.
Apply understanding of the volume formula for rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in figures and in context.
Apply understanding of the attributes of rectangular prisms to find an unknown dimension when given the volume.
Find the volume of solid figures with one-digit dimensions composed of two non-overlapping rectangular prisms in context.

topics.name: Line graphs and line plots
topics.description: Use the data cycle with line graphs, line plots and bar graphs. Covers questions about categorical data and data that change over time, planning and collecting, graphing, and drawing conclusions and predictions.
topics.statement: Apply the data cycle with a focus on line graphs, line plots, and bar graphs.

objectives.statement: Generate questions that require the collection of categorical or numerical data, including numerical data that change over time.
Determine whether a question will yield categorical or numerical data, including numerical data that change over time.
Design a plan to collect categorical or numerical data, including numerical data that change over time, to answer a question.
Collect categorical or numerical data, including numerical data that change over time, using various methods to answer a question.
Represent a data set by organizing and structuring collected data on a line graph, line plot, or bar graph.
Analyze categorical or numerical data to describe, compare, draw conclusions, and construct arguments supported by evidence from the data.
Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning to generalize and make predictions based on patterns and trends in the data.

topics.name: Ratios and unit ratios
topics.description: Understand equivalent ratios. Covers ratio language for part-to-part and part-to-whole, writing ratios in several notations, and the two unit ratios that relate two quantities.
topics.statement: Understand the concept of equivalent ratios.

objectives.statement: Make use of structure to describe the multiplicative relationships between the two quantities of a ratio, including part to part and part to whole relationships, using ratio language in context.
Represent a ratio relationship using ratio language, written expressions, colon, ratio tables, and fraction notation.
Reason quantitatively to determine the two distinct unit ratios that relate two quantities with reciprocal relationships.
Make sense of the two distinct unit ratios that relate two quantities in context.

topics.name: Ratio problems and percents
topics.description: Use ratio reasoning to solve problems, including percents. Covers ratio tables, double number lines and graphs, unit conversions, independent and dependent variables, percent as a rate per 100, and finding a part, whole or percent.
topics.statement: Apply ratio reasoning to represent and solve problems involving ratios and percentages using multiple representations.

objectives.statement: Construct tables and graphs to compare ratios composed of whole numbers.
Reason with patterns within ratio tables, double number lines, tape diagrams, contexts, and coordinate graphs to determine unknown values.
Reason quantitatively to manipulate measurements using given ratios for single unit conversions within the same measurement system.
Reason quantitatively to connect multiplicative relationships between independent and dependent variables in multiple representations.
Represent multiplicative relationships to solve problems with independent and dependent variables, using multiple representations.
Demonstrate an understanding of a percent as a ratio per 100 by expressing percents, using multiple representations.
Solve one-step problems determining an unknown part, whole, or percent of a given quantity, reasoning quantitatively with benchmark percentages or equivalent ratios.

topics.name: Factors and multiples
topics.description: Relate factors and multiples. Covers least common multiples, prime factorisation in exponent form, greatest common factors, and factoring a sum with the distributive property.
topics.statement: Determine the relationships between factors and multiples for mathematical problems.

objectives.statement: Reason quantitatively to determine the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12 for mathematical problems.
Make use of structure to rewrite whole numbers as products of their unique prime factors using exponential form when applicable.
Reason quantitatively to determine the greatest common factor of two whole numbers using strategies, including prime factorization, for mathematical problems.
Make use of structure to rewrite the sum of two whole numbers by using the distributive property and common factors.

topics.name: Fraction operations
topics.description: Operate with positive fractions and mixed numbers with denominators up to 12. Covers adding, subtracting and dividing with models, multiplying with an algorithm, interpreting quotients, word problems and checking reasonableness.
topics.statement: Apply numerical reasoning to perform operations with fractions with denominators 12 or less.

objectives.statement: Represent the sum, difference, and quotient of two positive fractions and mixed numbers, using physical and visual models, and common denominators.
Express repeated reasoning to evaluate the product of two positive fractions and mixed numbers using an algorithm.
Make sense of quotients and remainders of positive fractions and mixed numbers in terms of their context and relation to the divisor and dividend.
Solve problems by reasoning quantitatively with positive fractions and mixed numbers with the four operations.
Construct a viable argument for the reasonableness of solutions to contextual problems involving positive fractions and mixed numbers using estimation, mental math, and understanding of the context.

topics.name: Decimal operations
topics.description: Operate with positive decimals. Covers fluent algorithms for adding and subtracting to thousandths and multiplying and dividing to hundredths, estimation, and word problems.
topics.statement: Apply numerical reasoning to perform operations with positive decimals.

objectives.statement: Express repeated reasoning to evaluate the sum and difference of two decimals to the thousandths place, extending previous understandings to develop and fluently use an algorithm.
Express repeated reasoning to evaluate the product and quotient of two decimals to the hundredths place, extending previous understandings to develop and fluently use an algorithm.

Construct a viable argument for the reasonableness of a sum, difference, product, or quotient of two decimals using strategies to extend previous understandings, including estimation, mental math, and understanding of the context.
Solve problems involving decimals, reasoning quantitatively with the four operations.
Construct a viable argument for the reasonableness of solutions to contextual problems involving positive decimals using estimation, mental math, and understanding of the context.

topics.name: Integer operations
topics.description: Operate with integers from -20 to 20. Covers zero pairs, subtraction as adding the opposite, models for all four operations, computing, checking reasonableness, and problems in context.
topics.statement: Apply numerical reasoning to perform operations with integers within -20 and 20.

objectives.statement: Reason abstractly to describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make zero, conveying that a number and its additive inverse create a zero pair.

Make use of structure to represent the inverse relationship between addition and subtraction using multiple strategies, including physical and visual models. If p and q are integers, then p − q = p + (−q) and p + q = p − (−q).
Express repeated reasoning to represent addition and subtraction of two integers using models.
Express repeated reasoning to represent multiplication and division of two integers using models.
Evaluate the sum, difference, product, and quotient of two integers.
Construct a viable argument for the reasonableness of a sum, difference, product, or quotient of two integers in mathematical problems, using strategies including estimation and mental math.
Solve contextual problems reasoning quantitatively with the four operations involving integers, using efficient and flexible strategies.
Construct a viable argument for the reasonableness of solutions to contextual problems involving integers using estimation, mental math, and understanding of the context.

topics.name: Compare rational numbers
topics.description: Compare and order integers, fractions, mixed numbers and decimals. Covers equivalent forms, the number line, inequality statements, opposites, the meaning of zero, and absolute value.
topics.statement: Apply numerical reasoning to compare and order integers, fractions, mixed numbers, and decimals.

objectives.statement: Reason about the equivalence between rational numbers, using models and place value.
Make use of structure to locate and position rational numbers on a number line.
Make sense of statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two rational numbers on a number line.
Make sense of statements of order for rational numbers in context.
Reason abstractly to describe rational numbers having opposite directions or values in real-world context.

Demonstrate an understanding of the opposite signs of rational numbers as indicating locations on the opposite sides of zero, that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, and that zero is its own opposite.
Represent rational numbers in the real-world context, explaining the meaning of zero in each situation.
Make sense of the absolute value of rational numbers as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in context.

topics.name: Expressions and exponents
topics.description: Write and evaluate numerical and algebraic expressions. Covers whole-number exponents, order of operations, translating words to expressions, parts of an expression, evaluating, and equivalent expressions using properties.
topics.statement: Create and evaluate numerical and algebraic expressions.

objectives.statement: Demonstrate an understanding of whole-number exponents greater than zero.
Reason quantitatively to evaluate numerical expressions that may include whole number exponents greater than zero, using the order of operations with and without grouping symbols.
Construct numerical and algebraic expressions that may include whole number exponents greater than zero to solve problems.
Make use of structure to translate between mathematical expressions and written representations, with and without whole-number exponents.
Make use of structure to identify parts of an algebraic expression, with and without whole-number exponents, using mathematical terms.
Reason quantitatively to evaluate algebraic expressions, with or without whole number exponents, derived from problems.
Make use of structure to generate equivalent expressions, without exponents, using combining like terms and mathematical properties.

Construct a viable argument for the equivalence of two algebraic expressions using mathematical reasoning, combining like terms, and the commutative, associative, identity, and distributive properties.

topics.name: One-step equations and inequalities
topics.description: Represent and solve one-variable equations and represent inequalities. Covers checking solutions by substitution, writing and solving one-step equations, and writing and graphing simple inequalities.
topics.statement: Apply algebraic reasoning to represent one-variable equations and inequalities and solve one-variable equations using the four operations with positive fractions, positive decimals, and integers within -20 and 20.

objectives.statement: Construct a viable argument to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation true, using substitution.
Reason quantitatively to represent one-step equations to solve contextual problems.
Make use of structure and properties of equality to solve one-step equations.
Construct a viable argument for the reasonableness of the solution of one-step equations using estimation, mental math, and understanding of the context.
Construct a viable argument to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an inequality true, using substitution.
Make use of structure to translate between verbal descriptions and mathematical representations of inequalities of the form x > c, x > c, x < c, or x < c, given a constraint or condition.
Make use of structure to recognize that inequalities of the form x > c, x > c, x < c, or x < c have infinitely many solutions.
Represent solutions of inequalities of the form x > c, x > c, x < c or x < c on number line diagrams.
Construct a viable argument for the reasonableness of solutions of inequalities on number line diagrams.

topics.name: Area of polygons
topics.description: Solve problems about the area of two-dimensional figures. Covers areas of triangles, special quadrilaterals and polygons by composing and decomposing shapes, and checking answers in context.
topics.statement: Apply geometric reasoning to represent and solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the area of two-dimensional figures.

objectives.statement: Construct a model to find the area of a triangle using composition and decomposition of parallelograms.
Construct a model to find the area of a triangle using decomposition of special quadrilaterals and polygons.
Construct models to find the area of special quadrilaterals and polygons by decomposing them into triangles or rectangles.
Solve problems by extending structural understanding of areas of triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons, using efficient and flexible strategies.

Construct a viable argument for the solutions of contextual problems involving areas of two-dimensional figures by comparing different geometric representations, estimating or checking for reasonableness, and explaining how the result applies to the context.

topics.name: Four-quadrant coordinate plane
topics.description: Solve problems with the coordinate plane. Covers plotting points in all four quadrants, reflections across axes, distances between points sharing a coordinate, and polygons with perimeter and area.
topics.statement: Apply geometric reasoning to represent and solve real-world and mathematical problems using the coordinate plane.

objectives.statement: Make use of structure to identify the location of a point given as an ordered pair.
Make use of structure to graph ordered pairs in all four quadrants and axes of a coordinate plane to solve problems.
Make use of structure in recognizing that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes on a coordinate plane.
Reason quantitatively to determine the distances between points with the same x-coordinate or same y-coordinate, using coordinates and the absolute value of numbers.
Make use of structure to recognize and represent polygons in the coordinate plane, given coordinates for the vertices, to solve problems.

Determine the lengths of segments or the sides of a triangle or a quadrilateral on a coordinate plane, with the same x-coordinate or the same y-coordinate, to solve problems involving perimeter and area.

topics.name: Nets, surface area and volume
topics.description: Solve problems with surface area and volume. Covers nets of prisms and pyramids, surface area of rectangular and triangular prisms, and volume of rectangular prisms with fractional edges.
