topics.statement: Apply geometric reasoning to represent and solve problems involving surface area and volume of three-dimensional figures.

objectives.statement: Construct geometric nets, using rectangles and triangles, to build, recognize, and represent right prisms and right pyramids.
Solve problems involving the surface area of right rectangular and triangular prisms using nets, efficiently and flexibly.

Construct a viable argument for the solutions of contextual problems involving surface area of right rectangular and triangular prisms by comparing different geometric representations, estimating or checking for reasonableness, and explaining how the result applies to the context.
Solve problems by extending structural understanding of the volume of right rectangular prisms with rational edge lengths, efficiently and flexibly.

Construct a viable argument for the solutions of contextual problems involving volume of right rectangular prisms with rational edge lengths by comparing different geometric representations, estimating or checking for reasonableness, and explaining how the result applies to the context.

topics.name: Probability of simple events
topics.description: Investigate chance and the probability of simple, equally likely events. Covers probability language and values from 0 to 1, theoretical probability, and comparing experiments with theory.
topics.statement: Investigate chance processes and evaluate their probabilities for simple events and uniform (equally likely) probabilities.

objectives.statement: Construct a viable argument to describe the likelihood of a chance event using appropriate probability language and values from zero to one.
Reason quantitatively to determine the theoretical probability of a simple event with equally likely probabilities, comparing the number of favorable outcomes to the total number of outcomes.
Conduct experiments with simple events that have equally likely probabilities to compare the experimental results with the theoretical probabilities.

topics.name: Statistical questions and samples
topics.description: Pose and investigate statistical questions about one population. Covers telling statistical questions apart, spotting bias, collecting data from a representative sample, and organising it.
topics.statement: Formulate and investigate statistical questions to make inferences about univariate data for a population.

objectives.statement: Categorize statistical and non-statistical questions to investigate a topic of interest given a context for univariate data.

Construct a viable argument to determine whether a question is statistical or non-statistical by analyzing the presence of anticipated variability in the data and accounting for this variability in the answer.
Evaluate statistical questions and their results for potential bias when investigating univariate data in a single population.
Collect data on a single variable for a representative sample of a population.
Organize univariate data for a representative sample of a group or population using representations, accurately and clearly, when investigating a real-world topic of interest.

topics.name: Dot plots, histograms and box plots
topics.description: Examine numerical data displayed on a number line. Covers key features of line plots, histograms and box plots, constructing them, describing centre and spread, and reading non-standard displays.
topics.statement: Examine a set of numerical data in plots on a number line considering center and spread.

objectives.statement: Make use of structure to describe the key features in line plots, histograms, and box plots.
Reason quantitatively to describe what information can be deduced from line plots, histograms, and box plots, examining the center, spread, and shape.
Construct line plots, histograms, and box plots to represent a distribution of univariate data, by hand within 10 values and using technology within 25 values.
Make use of structure to describe measures of center represented in line plots, histograms, and box plots.
Make use of structure to describe variability represented in line plots, histograms, and box plots.
Make sense of non-standard data visualizations describing univariate data in a single population from real-world sources, describing what information is shown and what conclusions can be drawn.

topics.name: Mean and median
topics.description: Model and analyse a data set by its centre and spread. Covers the mean as a balance point, finding mean and median, comparing displays and variability, and choosing the best measure of centre.
topics.statement: Model and analyze a set of numerical data considering center and spread.

objectives.statement: Represent the mean as the balance point of data distributions using visual representations and physical models.
Determine mean and median for data distributions, by hand within 10 values and using technology within 25 values.

Make use of structure to compare line plots, histograms, and box plots of different data distributions displayed on the same scale with similar measures of center and different spreads to describe and interpret differences in variability.
Compare different representations of the same data distribution by analyzing their center, spread, and shape.
Construct a viable argument about which measure of center best represents a data distribution based on its shape and the context in which the data were gathered.

topics.name: Interpret a data investigation
topics.description: Summarise and interpret a one-variable data investigation. Covers drawing inferences from centre and variability, summarising a distribution, communicating findings, and reflecting on the question and methods.
topics.statement: Summarize and interpret results from an investigation (data cycle) of univariate data to make predictions and draw conclusions.

objectives.statement: Draw inferences about the overall pattern of a data distribution based on its measures of center and variability, its representation, and the context in which the data were gathered.
Summarize the distribution of univariate data by describing measures of center and variability, identifying overall patterns, and noting any striking deviations from the pattern.
Communicate findings using quantitative measures of center and variability, describing patterns, and noting how the findings relate to the context.
Reflect on findings to evaluate whether the original question and methods were appropriate, refining the investigative question, data collection plan, or analysis approach based on results.

topics.name: Unit rates and proportions
topics.description: Use the unit rate, or constant of proportionality, in proportional relationships. Covers identifying what stays constant, unit rates with fractions, testing for proportionality, representing and comparing relationships, and reading points in context.
topics.statement: Apply the concept of a unit rate (constant of proportionality) in proportional relationships.

objectives.statement: Reason quantitatively to determine invariant relationship(s) present in a problem.
Solve problems by reasoning quantitatively with unit rates, including those with ratios of fractions, using mathematical models and written descriptions.

Construct a viable argument for determining whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, given a situation involving unit rate (constant of proportionality), using multiple representations.
Represent proportional relationships using multiple representations.
Compare two different proportional relationships using multiple representations.
Make sense of any coordinate point of a proportional relationship in context.

topics.name: Scale drawings and percents
topics.description: Use proportional reasoning for scale and percent problems. Covers unit conversions, constructing and using scale drawings, how scale affects area, and tax, markups, tips, commission and percent change.
topics.statement: Apply proportional reasoning to solve scale and percent problems in context.

objectives.statement: Solve problems by converting one or both units reasoning quantitatively with unit rates or scale factors given the conversion ratios.
Construct scale drawings and models from actual lengths to determine that corresponding side lengths are proportional and corresponding angle measures are the same.
Solve problems with scale drawings of geometric figures by computing actual lengths and areas or constructing a scale drawing at a different scale.
Express repeated reasoning to determine the effect of scale factor on the area of scaled geometric figures.
Solve ratio and percent problems involving one or more steps by reasoning quantitatively with tax, markups/markdowns, tips, commissions, and percent increase/decrease.

topics.name: Circle graphs and circumference
topics.description: Use proportional reasoning with circles. Covers circle graphs in degrees, fractions and percents, the ratio of circumference to diameter as pi, and problems with radius, diameter and circumference.
topics.statement: Apply proportional reasoning to solve problems involving circles.

objectives.statement: Make sense of the part-to-whole relationships in circle graphs to relate degree measures in multiples of 30 and 45, benchmark fractional parts of circles in multiples of ¼ and ⅓, and benchmark percents.
Solve problems by reasoning quantitatively to connect degree measures with portions of the whole in circle graphs.
Reason quantitatively to demonstrate an understanding of the ratio relationship between circumference, pi (π), and diameter of a circle, using informal reasoning, visual models and physical models.
Solve problems involving the relationships between radius, diameter, and/or circumference of circles.

topics.name: Rational number operations
topics.description: Operate with integers, fractions and decimals. Covers rational numbers as quotients and as terminating or repeating decimals, fluent operations, checking reasonableness, and converting fractions to decimals.
topics.statement: Apply numerical reasoning to perform operations with integers, fractions and decimals.

objectives.statement: Construct a viable argument demonstrating a rational number can be expressed as a quotient of two integers and as a decimal that either terminates or repeats.

Express repeated reasoning to fluently evaluate the sum, difference, product, or quotient of rational numbers and/or absolute values of rational numbers, using the properties of operations by extending previous understandings of integer operations.

Construct a viable argument for the reasonableness of sums, differences, products, and quotients involving rational numbers and/or absolute values of rational numbers by using estimation, contextual reasoning, and previous understandings of integer operations.
Make use of structure to convert fractions to decimals to the thousandths place, extending previous understanding of division.

topics.name: Equivalent linear expressions
topics.description: Generate equivalent linear expressions with properties of operations. Covers factoring, combining like terms and the distributive property, and what equivalent forms reveal in context.
topics.statement: Apply algebraic reasoning to generate equivalent linear expressions using properties of operations.

objectives.statement: Make use of structure to generate equivalent linear expressions with rational coefficients by factoring, combining like terms, and using the distributive property and area model.
Construct a viable argument to demonstrate that equivalent expressions can represent and reveal mathematical and real-world relationships.
Make sense of the meaning of the parts of equivalent expressions in context to reveal real-world and mathematical relationships.

topics.name: Multi-step equations and inequalities
topics.description: Solve problems with expressions, equations and inequalities using rational numbers. Covers writing and solving multi-step equations and inequalities with the variable on one side, graphing solutions, and choosing between them.
topics.statement: Apply numeric and algebraic reasoning to solve problems involving expressions, equations, and inequalities with integers, fractions, and decimals.

objectives.statement: Reason quantitatively to fluently solve multi-step problems, using properties of operations of algebraic expressions to justify your solution process.
Construct multi-step equations with the same variable on one side of the equation to represent quantities and relationships in real-world problems.

Make use of structure and the properties of equality to solve multi-step equations with variables on one side of the equation, using flexible and efficient strategies.
Construct a viable argument for the reasonableness of the solutions of multi-step equations.

Make use of structure to represent solutions of inequalities with the same variable on one side of the inequality on number line diagrams.
Construct a viable argument for the reasonableness of the solution set of an inequality.
Construct a viable argument for determining whether an equation or inequality best represents the relationship between quantities in a contextual situation.

topics.name: Area of circles and composite figures
topics.description: Solve area problems with triangles, quadrilaterals, circles and polygons. Covers how circumference, pi and area relate, area of a circle, and perimeter and area of composite figures in context.
topics.statement: Apply geometric reasoning to solve problems involving areas of two-dimensional figures composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, circles, and polygons.

objectives.statement: Make use of structure to understand the relationships between circumference, pi (π), diameter, and area of a circle, using informal reasoning, visual and physical models.
Solve problems by reasoning quantitatively about the area of a circle when given the radius, diameter, or circumference.
Solve problems by reasoning quantitatively about the perimeter and area of two-dimensional figures composed of triangles, rectangles, and circles.

Construct a viable argument for the solutions of contextual problems involving area and perimeter of two-dimensional figures by comparing different geometric representations, estimating or checking for reasonableness, and explaining how the result applies to the context.

topics.name: Prisms and cylinders
topics.description: Solve problems with the surface area and volume of solids. Covers surface area as the sum of faces, volume as layers of the base, and problems with right prisms, cylinders and composite solids.
topics.statement: Apply geometric reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume and surface area of three-dimensional figures.

objectives.statement: Make use of structure to demonstrate an understanding of the surface area of right prisms and cylinders as the sum of the areas of the faces, using models.

Solve problems by reasoning quantitatively about the volume of right prisms, cylinders, or three-dimensional objects composed of cubes, cylinders, and right prisms, efficiently and flexibly.

Construct a viable argument for the solutions of contextual problems involving volume of right prisms and cylinders by comparing different geometric representations, estimating or checking for reasonableness, and explaining how the result applies to the context.

topics.name: Angle relationships
topics.description: Find unknown angles from angle relationships. Covers vertical, adjacent, supplementary and complementary angles, writing equations for unknown angles, and multi-step problems with intersecting lines.
topics.statement: Apply geometric reasoning based on angle relationships to determine unknown angles.

topics.name: Probability of compound events
topics.description: Investigate chance with compound events and unequal outcomes. Covers theoretical probability, sample spaces with lists, tables and tree diagrams, simulations, and how experiments approach theory as trials grow.
topics.statement: Investigate chance processes and evaluate their probabilities for compound events and unequally likely probabilities.

objectives.statement: Reason quantitatively to determine the theoretical probability of simple events with unequally likely outcomes as the ratio of favorable outcomes to total outcomes.

topics.name: Random samples and inference
topics.description: Pose and investigate statistical questions comparing two groups. Covers writing statistical questions, bias, why random samples represent a population, simulating samples, and organising data from two groups.

topics.name: Compare two data displays
topics.description: Examine two sets of numerical data on a number line. Covers comparing shape, centre and spread informally, plotting two distributions together, and reading non-standard displays.
topics.statement: Examine two sets of numerical data in plots on a number line considering the center and spread of univariate data.

objectives.statement: Make use of structure to compare two distributions of univariate data, informally examining the shape, center, and variability seen in given line plots, box plots, and/or histograms.

topics.name: Range, IQR and MAD
topics.description: Model and analyse the centre and spread of up to two data sets. Covers range, interquartile range and mean absolute deviation, choosing measures, comparing distributions, and the effect of extreme values.

objectives.statement: Represent range, interquartile range (IQR), and mean absolute deviation (MAD) as measures that describe the spread of data using visual representations and physical models.

topics.name: Compare two groups with data

topics.name: Equations with variables on both sides

topics.name: Introduction to functions

Make use of structure to determine where a function is increasing or decreasing and linear or non-linear when represented in a graph, table, or set of ordered pairs.

topics.name: Linear functions

topics.name: Irrational numbers
topics.description: Describe how the subsets of the real numbers relate. Covers recognising irrational numbers, placing and estimating them on a number line, and approximating expressions with pi.

objectives.statement: Reason quantitatively to categorize a number as irrational when it cannot be expressed as the ratio of two integers and its decimal expansion neither terminates nor repeats.

topics.name: Exponents, roots and scientific notation
topics.description: Develop properties of radicals and integer exponents. Covers exponent properties, square and cube roots, solving x² = p and x³ = p, and using and comparing numbers in scientific notation.
topics.statement: Develop and apply properties of radicals and integer exponents.

objectives.statement: Express repeated reasoning to generate equivalent numerical expressions using the properties of integer exponents.

topics.name: Conditions for a triangle

topics.name: Pyramids, cones and spheres
topics.description: Solve problems with the surface area and volume of solids. Covers surface area of pyramids, how volumes of cones, spheres and pyramids relate to cylinders and prisms, and volume problems.

topics.statement: Investigate mutually exclusive and inclusive events to determine probability.

topics.description: Evaluate weighted voting systems. Covers the Banzhaf and Shapley-Shubik power indices, coalitions using subsets and permutations, and the fairness of real systems.
topics.statement: Evaluate weighted voting systems.

objectives.statement: Analyze weighted voting systems using the Banzhaf and Shapley-Shubik power indices.
Analyze voting coalitions using subsets and permutations.
Critique the fairness and effectiveness of weighted voting systems in real-world contexts.

topics.name: Fair division
topics.description: Solve problems with fair-division methods. Covers divider-chooser, lone-divider, lone-chooser, sealed bids and markers, and weighing their strengths and fairness.
topics.statement: Analyze fair-division methods to solve problems.

objectives.statement: Determine equitable outcomes using fair-division strategies: divider-chooser, lone-divider, lone-chooser, sealed bids, and markers.
Assess the advantages, limitations, and fairness of various division methods, such as divider-chooser, lone-divider, lone-chooser, sealed bids, and markers, in context.

topics.name: Apportionment methods
topics.description: Evaluate methods for apportioning seats. Covers the Hamilton, Jefferson, Adams, Webster and Huntington-Hill methods and critiquing their fairness.
topics.statement: Evaluate apportionment methods.

objectives.statement: Analyze the distribution of seats among groups using the Hamilton, Jefferson, Adams, Webster, and Huntington-Hill apportionment methods.
Critique the fairness and effectiveness of apportionment methods in real-world contexts.

topics.name: Frame statistical questions
topics.description: Formulate and refine statistical questions that data can answer. Covers telling statistical questions apart, anticipating variability, refining questions for data and audience, and how framing shapes conclusions.
topics.statement: Formulate and refine statistical questions that can be addressed with data by connecting context, purpose, and variability.

objectives.statement: Distinguish between statistical and non-statistical questions.
Formulate investigable statistical questions that anticipate variability in data.
Refine questions iteratively to align with data availability, context, and intended audience.
Explain how the way a statistical question is framed influences the variables studied, the type of data collected, and the conclusions that can be drawn from the investigation.

topics.name: Design studies and surveys
topics.description: Design and carry out data collection that limits bias. Covers random sampling in surveys and observational studies, random assignment in experiments, ethics, neutral instruments, and collecting with technology.
topics.statement: Design and carry out data collection plans that use randomization, limit bias, and support valid conclusions that address a statistical question.

objectives.statement: Design observational studies and surveys using random sampling to minimize bias.
Design experiments with random assignment to control for confounding variables and minimize bias.
Justify choices in study design by considering ethical principles, including informed consent, fair representation of groups, and the avoidance of unfair treatment.
Create data collection instruments (e.g., survey questions and observational tools) with neutral wording, structure, and visuals that minimize bias and support data validity.
Use technology to collect data efficiently.

topics.name: Sampling methods
topics.description: Understand how sampling affects whether a sample represents a population. Covers populations versus samples, why we sample, random sampling, choosing a method, and how bias affects validity.
topics.statement: Understand that different sampling methods affect how well a sample represents a population and contribute to a valid conclusion.

objectives.statement: Explain the difference between populations and samples.
Describe the purpose of sampling when drawing conclusions about the population.
Use random sampling to select a representative sample from a population.
Construct a viable argument for using a sampling method for a given situation.
Explain how randomization and sampling bias affect the validity of the results of a study.

topics.name: Collect and clean data
topics.description: Collect and prepare original and secondary data for analysis. Covers generating data, compiling and organising existing data, cleaning datasets, and noting limitations and sources of bias.
topics.statement: Collect and process original and secondary data so they are ready for analysis and interpretation.

objectives.statement: Generate original data using designed surveys, observational tools, experiments, and simulations.
Compile secondary data from pre-existing data sources.
Organize secondary data into appropriate structures.
Clean collected datasets (original and secondary) for analysis by addressing missing values, combining datasets, and creating new variables when appropriate.
Critique the assumptions and limitations of original and secondary data and note possible sources of error, bias, or misrepresentation.

topics.name: Data ethics
topics.description: Apply fairness, consent and representation when collecting data. Covers informed consent and the right to withdraw, risks of misrepresentation, and justifying ethical collection choices.
topics.statement: Apply principles of fairness, consent, and representation when creating and collecting data.

objectives.statement: Explain the principles of informed consent, voluntary participation, and the right to withdraw.
Analyze risks of misrepresentation and bias introduced through collection practices.
Justify decisions about data creation and collection in light of ethical and civic responsibilities.

topics.name: Create data visualizations
topics.description: Visualise multivariate data to find patterns and compare distributions. Covers choosing a display for the data and audience, building it with technology, and reading its key features.
topics.statement: Create visualizations of multivariate data to identify patterns, compare distributions, and support analysis.

objectives.statement: Select appropriate visualizations based on data type, context, and audience.
Construct visualizations of multivariate data using technology.
Interpret the key features of data visualizations.

topics.name: Critique data visualizations
topics.description: Critique and improve visualizations. Covers how scales, axes, order, colour and aggregation affect reading, what different displays highlight, revising for clarity and accessibility, and judging published graphics.
topics.statement: Critique and refine visualizations for accuracy, clarity, and appropriateness.

objectives.statement: Analyze how design decisions affect the interpretation of data, including scales, axes, ordering, color, and aggregation.
Explain how different data visualizations highlight varying aspects of a data narrative.
Revise visualizations to improve clarity, transparency, and accessibility.
Evaluate visualizations in the media and research for accuracy and fairness.

topics.name: Descriptive statistics
topics.description: Summarise and compare distributions with descriptive statistics. Covers choosing numerical summaries, interpreting them in context, comparing centre, shape and spread, and measures of relative standing.
topics.statement: Summarize, analyze, and compare multivariate distributions using descriptive statistics.

objectives.statement: Summarize a data set with appropriate numerical measures that describe the distribution.
Interpret measures of multivariate distributions in context.
Compare measures of centrality, shape, and spread for two or more multivariate distributions in context.
Interpret measures of relative standing.

topics.name: Statistical and probability models
topics.description: Build and interpret models that describe data. Covers linear, exponential, quadratic and logistic models, parameters, residual plots, choosing a model, binomial and normal distributions, and z-scores.
topics.statement: Build mathematical and probabilistic models that describe data and interpret them in context.

objectives.statement: Create linear, exponential, quadratic, and logistic models using technology.
Interpret model parameters in context.
Evaluate the goodness of fit of nonlinear models by analyzing residual plots.
Justify model selection based on purpose and context.
Determine when it is appropriate to model datasets with a binomial or normal distribution.
Calculate probabilities of events modeled by a binomial distribution.
Calculate probabilities of events modeled by a normal distribution using technology.
Compare data points from normal distributions that have different means and standard deviations using z-scores.

topics.name: Randomness and simulation
topics.description: Use probability and random processes to model uncertainty. Covers the role of probability, simulation to estimate a mean or proportion with a margin of error, and testing differences between groups.
topics.statement: Understand the role of randomness in data by applying probability and random processes as models of uncertainty.

objectives.statement: Explain the role of probability in modeling randomness and uncertainty.
Explain how simulation can be used to estimate a population mean or proportion and to determine a margin of error for the estimate.
Determine, using simulation, whether observed differences between samples from two populations provide evidence that the populations differ with respect to a parameter of interest.

topics.name: Present data insights
topics.description: Communicate data insights to different audiences. Covers presentations that combine visuals with narrative and probabilistic language, and adapting the message to the audience.
topics.statement: Communicate insights using data visualizations through narratives and presentations tailored to varied audiences.

objectives.statement: Develop data presentations that integrate visualizations with narrative explanations that include probabilistic and contextual language.
Adapt communication to a specific audience by highlighting relevant context.

topics.name: Inference from samples
topics.description: Draw and justify inferences about a population from sample data. Covers limits on generalising, informal inference by simulation, margins of error, and judging predicted values.
topics.statement: Draw and justify inferences from sample data about a population by using probabilistic reasoning.

objectives.statement: Explain how limitations in sampling influence the extent to which results can be generalized.
Make informal inferences, using randomization and simulation, about population parameters.
Interpret margins of error as measures of uncertainty when making inferences about population parameters.
Assess the validity of a predicted value.

topics.name: Evaluate data-based claims
topics.description: Critique claims based on data and the limits of inference. Covers evidence from observational studies versus experiments and critiquing claims in media, research and policy.
topics.statement: Evaluate and critique claims based on data, recognizing the limitations of statistical inference.

objectives.statement: Evaluate the strength and limitations of evidence from observational studies versus experiments.
Critique claims in the media, research, and policy by analyzing data sources, study design, and reasoning.

topics.name: The modeling process
topics.description: Solve and defend real-world problems with the modeling cycle. Covers identifying a problem, naming quantities and assumptions, building and analysing a model, testing conjectures, revising, and explaining and critiquing models.
topics.statement: Find and defend solutions to real-world scenarios using the mathematical modeling process.

objectives.statement: Identify a real-world scenario that requires analysis.
Describe the essential quantities, relationships, assumptions, constraints, and questions in a mathematical situation.
Decontextualize the mathematical situation to construct a model.
Use appropriate tools to analyze the model.
Make conjectures and explore their validity using mathematics.
Recontextualize the conclusion to determine appropriateness and to modify the model as needed.
Construct a viable argument that details the steps for creating and modifying the model and drawing conclusions.
Critique the reasoning used in another's modeling process and solution.

topics.name: Choose a function type
topics.description: Analyse patterns of change to choose a function model. Covers picking a function type from a context, defining variables and parameters, and a reasonable domain and range.
topics.statement: Look for and make use of structure to analyze patterns of change across different function types.

objectives.statement: Identify the appropriate function type to model in a context based on patterns of change.
Identify and define independent variables, dependent variables, and constant parameters within real-world scenarios.
Determine a reasonable domain and range for a function in context.

topics.name: Build function models
topics.description: Represent situations with polynomial, exponential, reciprocal, piecewise or logarithmic functions. Covers building polynomial and piecewise models, regression with technology, useful representations, and justifying the model chosen.
topics.statement: Decontextualize a mathematical situation by representing it with a polynomial, exponential, reciprocal, piecewise, or logarithmic function as part of the mathematical modeling process.

objectives.statement: Use appropriate tools to build a polynomial function that models the key features of a real-world scenario.
Build a piecewise function from a situation or graph.
Use technology to build polynomial and logarithmic regression models.
Use appropriate representations to highlight key features of and solutions to a mathematical situation.
Justify the model selected to represent a mathematical situation.

topics.name: Interpret function models
topics.description: Interpret a model's key features and solutions in context. Covers inputs and outputs, solving equations and inequalities with technology, and key features of several function families.
topics.statement: Recontextualize the key features of and the solutions to equations and inequalities from a model as part of the mathematical modeling process.

objectives.statement: Interpret the inputs and outputs of functions in context.
Solve equations from a function model using appropriate technology.
Solve inequalities from a model using appropriate technology.
Interpret the key features of polynomial, exponential, reciprocal, piecewise, and logarithmic functions.
Interpret solutions to equations and inequalities in context.

topics.name: Plan a statistical investigation
topics.description: Pose statistical questions and plan how to collect data. Covers writing questions, designing surveys and samples, anticipating variability, collecting and curating data, and noting limits and bias.
topics.statement: Formulate and investigate statistical questions about real-world issues to make inferences about data as part of the statistical modeling process.

objectives.statement: Construct statistical questions to guide explorations of data in context.
Design surveys using sampling methods to collect data aligned with a statistical question.
Use informal or theoretical probability to anticipate possible outcomes and variability.
Implement plans to collect and curate original and/or existing data.
Explain the limitations and uncertainty associated with the collected data.
Evaluate statistical questions for potential sources of bias in data collection or response.

topics.name: Explore and summarize data
topics.description: Explore collected data to investigate a question. Covers visualising quantitative and categorical data, reading displays, calculating and interpreting summaries, and comparing patterns with chance.
topics.statement: Explore and evaluate collected data to investigate a statistical question as part of the statistical modeling process.

objectives.statement: Create data visualizations using technology to represent quantitative and categorical data.
Interpret key features of graphical representations of data.
Calculate numerical summaries of quantitative and categorical data.
Interpret numerical summaries of quantitative and categorical data.
Recognize when observed patterns align with or differ from expected probabilistic behavior.

topics.name: Probability distributions for decisions
topics.description: Use probability distributions to make decisions under uncertainty. Covers discrete, binomial and normal models, finding likelihoods, and justifying decisions with probability.
topics.statement: Apply probability distributions to make decisions under uncertainty as part of the statistical modeling process.

objectives.statement: Create probability models using discrete, binomial, and normal distributions.
Determine the likelihood of events occurring using discrete, binomial, and normal distributions.
Make decisions using probability models.
Construct a viable argument to support decisions using probabilistic reasoning.

topics.name: Nonlinear regression models
topics.description: Analyse relationships in multivariate data. Covers polynomial, exponential and logarithmic regression, judging fit with residuals, r and r², and drawing evidence-based conclusions.
topics.statement: Analyze relationships in multivariate datasets using statistical measures as part of the statistical modeling process.

objectives.statement: Construct polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic regression models for bivariate data using technology to model data and solve problems.
Compare residuals, residual plots, the correlation coefficient, and the coefficient of determination for nonlinear models to assess model goodness of fit.
Draw conclusions that answer the statistical question using evidence based on the analysis of the statistical model.

topics.name: Communicate statistical findings
topics.description: Summarise and communicate a statistical modeling investigation. Covers evaluating questions, plans and probability models, presenting conclusions with limitations, and critiquing other investigations.
topics.statement: Summarize findings from the statistical modeling process and communicate the workflow and conclusions.

objectives.statement: Evaluate the appropriateness of the investigative questions, data collection plan, or analysis approach based on results.

Communicate conclusions about data through narratives and presentations that describe the statistical modeling process used, including discussion of the limitations of the data, potential sources of bias, and additional questions that emerged.
Evaluate the appropriateness of probability models used to represent the situation.
Critique the workflow, conclusions, and potential sources of bias in data investigations by analyzing data sources, sampling design, and reasoning.
